newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves alumina venture with foreign equity.
newsitem.headline: India approves alumina venture with foreign equity.

text.p: The Indian cabinet approved on Friday a proposal by Gujarat Alumina and Bauxite Ltd (GABL) to set up an alumina plant with foreign equity of 1.628 billion rupees ($45.4 million), the government said in a statement.
The cabinet approved the foreign equity, which would form 22 percent of a total paid-up capital of 7.4 billion rupees ($206.7 million), the government said.
The state-run Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Ltd (GACL) and Gujarat Mineral Dev. Corpn Ltd formed the joint venture with Raytheon Engineers and Constructors of the United States.
The venture will set up facilities to make alumina, metallurgical coke, power and desalinated water, it said.

Raytheon will be the financial collaborator and Reynolds International of the U.S. the technical collaborator for the project which will be set up in the Kutch district in the western state of Gujarat, the government said.
